description: Look up a list of addresses in one call, returning a map keyed by address so duplicates collapse and the order you passed them stops mattering. Each answer is what `lookup_ip` gives for that address. Pass the whole list rather than splitting it yourself: a long one is batched for you. Prefer this over repeated `lookup_ip` calls when you already have the list, for example when triaging a log file. To check the agents such a log claims, pass `user_agents`, one `User-Agent` per address, and each answer says whether its address bears its agent out. A batch needs a key on a paid plan: with a key on the free plan, a list of up to 10 addresses is looked up one address at a time instead, and a longer one comes back refused. An address that fails carries its error in place of a result rather than failing the batch. Always read `coverage.note` before concluding anything from a field that is not in the result.

ips.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 addresses to look up.

user_agents.description: Each address's `User-Agent`, keyed by the address as `ips` spells it. An address left out sends none. The answer's `user_agent` then names the agent and says whether this address bears it out, so a crawler forging its agent reads `spoofed`. An answer without `user_agent` did not check the agent, which is no verdict either way.
